answer: Proof of Personhood protocols utilize cryptographic attestations to ensure each node represents a unique human, effectively walling off an island of authentic agents from automated spam. Much like a falcon surveying the vast tundra to identify prey, these networks scan for unique biometric signatures or social graph clusters. An attacker seeking to flood the system must incur the prohibitive cost of acquiring verified human identities, rendering the deployment of mass Sybil nodes economically unsustainable.
